name: Bloodline Disciples
body:
The Dragon Disciple is a great prestige class, and sorcerers/bloodragers of different bloodlines should have the opportunity to explore their inheritance as thoroughly as the progeny of dragons. Some general rules can be devised to adapt the class for descendants of different creatures; one example is the Crone Disciple, that is a good prestige class for both witches and sorcerers with the Accursed bloodline. So let’s try to imagine which requisites a “bloodline disciple” should have.

This is more than a simple prestige archetype and maybe something less than an alternate class: it’s a template that can be reused to adapt the dragon disciple chassis to any bloodline you like.

Table 1: Bloodline Disciple’s Hit Dice
Hit Die	Bloodlines
d6	Aberrant, arcane, fey, naga, psychic
d8	Aquatic, black blood, boreal, destined, dreamspun, ghoul, harrow, imperious, kobold, maestro, martyred, nanite, orc, possessed, scorpion, serpentine, shapechanger, solar, starsoul, undead, verdant, vestige
d10	Abyssal, accursed, astral, celestial, daemon, deep earth, div, djinni, ectoplasm, efreeti, elemental, hag, impossible, infernal, kyton, marid, medusa, oni, pestilence, phoenix, protean, rakshasa, salamander, shadow, shaitan, sphinx, stormborn, unicorn
d12	Draconic
Alignment: This should be required only in case the prestige class is strongly bent towards a specific vision of the world. Nothing bars a celestial sorcerer from being evil, for example, but if she chooses to explore her abilities in service of good-aligned planes as a celestial disciple, she should probably be good.
Hit Die: A bloodline disciple should use the same hit die of the creature he descends from. If the bloodline doesn’t derive from a specific kind of creature, it should use a d8 as a default.
Requirements: Don’t select too many requirements. 4-6 among the following are recommended.
Race: The bloodline disciple should not belong to the same creature type and/or subtype as the creature his bloodline derives from (if any). If a bloodline requires a character to belong to a certain race (like the kobold or imperious bloodline), then the bloodline disciple should abide by the same restrictions.
Gender: Gender restrictions may apply if the monster that the bloodline disciple tries to emulate has a prevailing gender or individuals of one gender only, like hags or medusas.
Feats/Skills: 5 ranks in the Knowledge skill required to identify creatures tied to the related bloodline. Knowledge (arcana) or Knowledge (religion) may be preferred for monsters with strong magic powers or bloodlines strongly tied to arcane or divine traditions. The relevant bloodline skill can also be selected. If there are some feats particularly fit for a tradition or always selected by a particular monster, these can be requirements too.
Languages: If there is tongue tied to the creature or tradition his bloodline derives from, the bloodline disciple should know it as a prerequisite.
Spellcasting: A bloodline disciple should be able to cast 1stlevel spells. Sorcerers and bloodragers should always be able to become disciples of their bloodline.
Other/Special: Other classes that can access the prestige class should be chosen so as to be thematically fit. It makes sense to let clerics and oracles become celestial disciples, witches become hag disciples, or druids become elemental or verdant disciples. Special requirements should be selected in order to allow access only to members of the selected classes.
Skills: Choose 6-8 thematically fit skills (different Craft, Knowledge, Perform, and Profession skills count as one for this purpose). You can select from the class skills of a specific monster type or character class. If you put a skill among the class prerequisites, this must be included.
Skill Ranks at Each Level: Every bloodline disciple gains 2 skill ranks per level + his Int modifier.
Base Attack Bonus: All bloodline disciples have a medium progression for base attack bonus (¾).
Saving Throws: Bloodline disciples have two good saves depending on their bloodline. The table below offers a quick reference.
Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Bloodline disciples gain no proficiency with any weapon or armor.

Spellcasting

A bloodline disciple with a d10 or d12 for his hit die should have a 7/10 spell progression. A bloodline disciple whose hit die is a d8 should have a 9/10 spell progression, and one whose hit die is a d6 should have a full 10/10 spell progression.

Bloodline Powers

Every bloodline disciple adds his level to his sorcerer or bloodrager levels when determining the powers gained from his bloodline. If the Dragon Disciple does not have levels in sorcerer or bloodrager, he instead gains sorcerer bloodline powers of his bloodline, using his bloodline disciple level as his sorcerer level to determine the bonuses gained.

Natural Armor Increase (Ex)

At 1st, 4th, and 7th level, all bloodline disciples gain a +1 increase to their existing natural armor (if any). These armor bonuses stack.

Table 2: Bloodline Disciple’s Good Saves
Bloodline	Good Saves
Aberrant, abyssal, black blood, boreal, celestial, deep earth, destined, div, djinni, draconic, efreeti, elemental, ghoul, imperious, impossible, infernal, kyton, marid, martyred, naga, oni, pestilence, possessed, protean, salamander, shaitan, solar, starsoul, stormborn, undead, verdant, vestige	Fort, Will
Accursed, arcane, astral, daemon, dreamspun, ectoplasm, fey, hag, harrow, kobold, maestro, medusa, nanite, rakshasa, psychic, shapechanger	Ref, Will
Aquatic, phoenix, scorpion, serpentine, shadow, sphinx, unicorn	Fort, Ref
Ability Boost (Ex)

At 2nd, 4th, 6th, and 8th level, a bloodline disciple gains a +2 increase in an ability score. Which ability scores to boost is a delicate choice. Choose 2 physical scores and 1 mental score, or 2 mental scores and 1 physical score, that seem most fit for the creature or tradition the bloodline derives from. One score should get a total +4 increase, while the other 2 should get a +2 increase. Charisma, or other spellcasting stats that classes with access to the prestige class could benefit from, should never receive more than a +2 boost. The table below offers a quick reference.

Bloodline Feats

Bloodline disciples gain a bonus feat at 2nd, 5th, and 8th level, chosen from their bloodline’s bonus feats list.

Enhanced Bloodline Powers

At 2nd level, a bloodline disciple gains an enhanced version of his 1st-level bloodline power. At 3rd level, he gains the 9th-level power from his bloodline (or the 8th-level power if he’s a bloodrager), and at 9th level, the 15th-level power from his bloodline (or the 12th-level power if he’s a bloodrager). If he already possesses or later gains these powers from his bloodline, he instead receives an enhanced version of these. Enhanced bloodline powers should typically make a character more similar to the monster he is emulating, either granting a special attack or a new movement form, or mutating his physical shape.

Sensory Ability (Ex)

At 5th level, the bloodline disciple gains a sensory ability normally possessed by the monster he is emulating. At 10th level, this is further empowered.

Table 3: Bloodline Disciple’s Ability Boosts

Aberrant	+4 Con, +2 Dex, +2 Int
Abyssal, div, possessed	+4 Str, +2 Con, +2 Wis

Destined, impossible, medusa, nanite, shadow	+4 Con, +2 Int, +2 Wis
Djinni, efreeti, elemental (air, fire, water), marid, salamander, stormborn	+4 Dex, +2 Str, +2 Wis
Draconic	+4 Str, +2 Con, +2 Int
Dreamspun, scorpion, shapechanger, starsoul	+4 Dex, +2 Wis, +2 Cha
Ectoplasm	+4 Dex, +2 Str, +2 Int

Table 4: Bloodline Forms
Level	Equivalent Spells
3rd	aberrant form I, beast shape I, elemental body I, fey form I, lesser proxy aspect, monstrous physique I, tree shape, undead anatomy I, vermin shape I
5th	beast shape III, elemental body II, monstrous physique II, ooze form I, plant shape I, undead anatomy II, vermin shape II
7th	aberrant form II, beast shape IV, elemental body III, fey form II, form of the dragon I, giant form I, plant shape Ii, proxy aspect, monstrous physique III, ooze form II, undead anatomy III
10th	aberrant form III, elemental body IV, fey form III, form of the dragon II, giant form II, greater proxy aspect, magical beast shape, monstrous physique IV, ooze form III, plant shape III, undead anatomy IV
Bloodline Form (Sp)

As his level increases, the bloodline disciple whose bloodline emulates a monster becomes able to assume the form of that monster. Some instances of this ability can replace some enhanced bloodline powers or sensorial abilities that wouldn’t fit right. At 3rd level, the disciple’s bloodline shape can be used once per day; at 7th level, twice per day; and at 10th level, three times per day. Use the table below as a help to select the equivalent spells for this ability.

Other/Variants: A bloodline disciple class should be further personalized by adding or replacing some features with others more thematically fit (as in the case of bloodline shape abilities replacing enhanced bloodline powers). This is the less mechanical and more artistic part of the template. It would make little sense for a destined disciple to assume the shape of a monster, for example, while he could find more useful a few cavalier or samurai abilities like banner or resolve, or the ability to gather followers as with Leadership. The Crone Disciple waives bloodline abilities and bloodline feats, stacking instead levels in the prestige class with levels in a class that grants hexes; it also grants transformation at 10th level only, but allowing to assume all the abilities of a real hag. It would be appropriate giving an alignment aura to disciples of strongly aligned bloodlines, like abyssal, celestial, and infernal, or even unicorn or phoenix.

Bloodline disciples that use a d8 or d6 as their hit die should be granted one or two additional class features as compared to bloodline disciples that use a d10 or d12.

Since reading the template could be difficult and requires some experience in class creation, a couple examples of new bloodline disciple prestige classes follow.
